rationale: ⚠️ The activation route consistently accompanies singular user mutation routes in the router. The contract's plural users/activation path appears to be a documentation typo.
⚠️ Event filters are a JSON request object; streaming media types describe the response. The contract appears to have copied response media types into consumes.
⚠️ Concurrent modification can exhaust deletion retries, appropriately yielding conflict. The deletion response list omits this supported outcome.
⚠️ A malformed target cannot establish permission verification. The error helper writes a failure body without setting a failure HTTP status, allowing an erroneous successful verification status.
⚠️ Invoice generation failure lacks the return used by the earlier error branch. Both response helpers serialize immediately, so execution falls through to a contradictory success response.

⚠️ Renamed fields have explicit model-to-DTO mappings but no corresponding DTO-to-model mappings. Creation calls that incomplete reverse mapper, losing fields the request representation deliberately exposes.
⚠️ The deliberate configurable message-length guard has a documented code default of 4000. The request schema omits that operational constraint, leaving clients unable to predict rejection.
⚠️ Authorization and reference checks concern the supplied context, but deletion selects only assetId. Missing ownership validation permits deletion outside that authorized context.
⚠️ Deletion deliberately parses tuple-selection filters, also represented by query parameter annotations. The generated delete operation omits the parameters needed to describe this behavior.
⚠️ Database absence is explicitly translated to resource-not-found, then indiscriminately converted to HTTP 500. The handler should preserve the contract's missing-resource outcome.
⚠️ The operation is intentionally registered in the administrator-only group, separately from public language options. The contract omits its authentication requirement.

⚠️ BlankResult deliberately represents an unresolved flag with ID zero and diagnostic context within a successful batch. The response schema's positive-only ID constraint excludes this designed fallback.
⚠️ Omission deliberately selects the configured global depth limit. Marking max-depth required contradicts that explicit defaulting behavior.
⚠️ The response count explicitly includes suppressed vulnerabilities while its findings list excludes them. The implementation uses inconsistent populations for the body and its total header.
⚠️ The code explicitly defines the UI/evaluation catalog as enabled enrichers of either scope. The contract's unqualified inclusion of flag-scoped enrichers overstates that effective catalog.
⚠️ Glob is explicitly provisioned alongside exact and regex in both the flavor list and storage schema. The contract's flavor description is incomplete.
⚠️ Multipart BOM uploads dispatch ScanUploadEvent to the dependency-check parser, whereas BOM processing supports the advertised CycloneDX/SPDX formats. The upload branch selects the wrong event.
⚠️ The handler loops exclusively over flagIDs, so a valid flagKeys-only request yields no evaluations. The advertised alternate identifier input is unimplemented.
⚠️ Request conversion preserves PurgeOnDelete, but response conversion copies the other cleanup fields and omits it. Reading configuration therefore loses an explicitly supplied boolean.
⚠️ Issuer failure bypasses the structured introspection error writer used immediately afterward. Its generic plain-text helper violates the endpoint's JSON error representation.
⚠️ The route computes cluster connectivity and returns the dedicated clusterSummary envelope. The controller-status response annotation appears copied from a different operation.
⚠️ Listing command capabilities is a read-only retrieval, and the resource explicitly registers GET. The contract's POST method is the likely documentation error.
⚠️ The evaluation code deliberately returns a diagnostic blank result when a flag cannot be resolved. The schema fails to admit its zero-ID sentinel.
⚠️ Organization-key collection and individual operations consistently use singular org in the router. The contract's plural orgs path is inconsistent with that deliberate route family.
⚠️ Routing deliberately separates the slashless listing from slash-prefixed file retrieval. The listing annotation and generated contract add a slash that selects the wrong handler.
⚠️ Tag deletion belongs to the explicitly authenticated mutation routes. The operation documentation omits the authentication requirement enforced for that group.
⚠️ Query parsing and SQL construction deliberately allow namespace-free tuple searches. The contract incorrectly marks this optional selection filter required.
⚠️ The contract's own URL template names hash, as do the route and handler. Only the parameter annotation says thumb, making it a clear specification naming error.
⚠️ Updating a nonexistent target produces an explicit unknown-process error. The handler collapses it into generic bad request instead of the advertised not-found response.
⚠️ Shared request parsing intentionally rejects malformed query encoding before endpoint dispatch. The operation's response list omits that legitimate client-error outcome.
⚠️ Retrieving interface configuration needs no comment-creation payload. The unrelated AddCommentReq body annotation is a documentation copy error.
⚠️ The mapper deliberately publishes the enabled catalog used by UI and evaluation. The contract should qualify flag-scoped entries by enablement as well as built-ins.

⚠️ POST persistence replaces fields and explicitly clears a null parent; a separate PATCH operation preserves omitted values. The POST documentation appears to incorrectly promise the partial-update parent semantics.
⚠️ A references endpoint returns the dedicated referencing-components envelope. Its ordinary controller-service response annotation describes the wrong operation and should be corrected.
⚠️ The endpoint searches labels with count and offset and returns a typed result slice. The single-object schema omits the array container appropriate to this listing.
⚠️ Successful credential login returns a user without recording USER_ID_KEY. Other session authentication paths store that key and subsequent session retrieval depends on it.
⚠️ Object and relation are deliberately optional query filters, applied only when nonempty. The contract incorrectly requires both for a tuple-query endpoint.
⚠️ Filtering builds an uninitialized result slice and leaves it nil when nothing matches. Serializing that value yields null rather than the promised empty policy array.
⚠️ The users resource retrieves User records. Referencing Position in its list schema is an unrelated model selection error.
⚠️ The mutation deletes by constraintID alone, ignoring segmentID and flag membership. Passing flagID to mutation bookkeeping does not constrain the actual deletion predicate.
⚠️ The response mapper omits PurgeOnDelete while copying sibling cleanup fields, although request mapping preserves it. Returning stored configuration consequently changes a true setting to false.
⚠️ Deletion selects the segment solely by its ID. The nested flagID affects mutation bookkeeping but never verifies that the selected segment belongs to that flag.
⚠️ The DAO retrieves all matches and the manager wraps them directly as PaginatedResult. No outer offset or limit selects the requested page, so advertised pagination is ineffective.
⚠️ The code defines and deliberately returns a named keys envelope. The response schema describes only its inner array and omits that wrapper.

⚠️ The supplied authorization callback checks the target context, affected components, and service references but omits inherited-context read checks. Referencing another context should require the advertised permission.
⚠️ HEAD verification uses a handler whose malformed-URL error branch never sets a failure status. Failed verification can therefore appear successful through the HTTP status alone.
⚠️ The router deliberately assigns listing to the slashless filesystem root and file retrieval to slash-prefixed paths. The contract's trailing slash points at the file route.
⚠️ Copying false into a value struct loses the distinction between an omitted filter and enabled=false. The supplied ORM explicitly excludes blank boolean fields from predicates.
⚠️ sitemap.html renders an HTML view through an HTML-configured resolver. Its text/plain declaration is inconsistent with the page's explicit format and rendering path.
⚠️ The router consistently exposes organization-key operations under singular org, including DELETE. The specification's plural orgs path is a route documentation error.

⚠️ PATCH merges the public DTO and passes it to toModel, but renamed fields have mappings only in the opposite direction. Submitted display name, homepage, and redirects cannot update their model properties.
⚠️ Position exposes a structured Network bean with multiple network properties. The contract's string type fails to represent that deliberate model structure.
⚠️ Streaming chat intentionally enforces the configurable message limit before opening the stream. The request schema omits the constraint and its default, making accepted message length misleading.
⚠️ The router and removal handler consistently identify one member in the path. The contract retains a collection path and body parameter that the implementation never consumes.
⚠️ The writer explicitly names metadata query_time, record_count, and page_size and exposes tags as labels. The specification describes different field names, likely a stale response shape.
⚠️ No matching roles leaves the filter result as a nil slice. The writer receives that value without normalization, producing null instead of the documented empty array.
⚠️ Route reports return Position beans whose network property is a structured Network bean. The specification's string declaration is inconsistent with the exposed model.
⚠️ Both the operation summary and entity method describe all share links. The response annotation/schema incorrectly models one Link instead of the returned collection.
⚠️ Image lookup translates missing rows into resource-not-found, but the endpoint maps every lookup error to HTTP 500. Missing artifacts should retain the documented 404 classification.
⚠️ Glob is an explicitly enabled and provisioned policy flavor, and deletion accepts it through the shared parser. The contract's two-flavor description is incomplete.
⚠️ Canceling a listing request returns its ListingRequestDTO in the dedicated listing envelope. DropRequestEntity belongs to queue-dropping operations, making this response annotation a copy error.
